record_notes.DCP-LETT-1815: January 3, supplied 1856; all nine blocks, twelve notes and bibliography read. Replies to missing Fox information on eggs, duck colour, sheep and seeds. Seeks old Cochin, Dorking, Malay and Call Drake; Call Drake was inserted above Malay without punctuation, not a Malay duck breed. Most outside specimens still promises, though more than twenty requests sent. Future Baily approach conditional; Athenaeum subscription ceased. Isle of Wight seed account lacks contemporaneous particulars/species certainty, not established evidence. Muscovy eggs requested in PS. Same old-cock request is also in October 1855 letter 1766, so March Fox response cannot be tied uniquely to this repetition by species names alone.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1646: March 8, supplied 1856 despite low catalogue ID; all nine blocks, nine notes, separate annotations and bibliography read. Search for old Dorking/Cochin and letter to Hornby reported, specimens not yet known received. Sebright Bantam offered, not dispatched. Hound story distinguishes prior belief, observed cross-back producing a deerhound-like puppy, anecdote about recognition in London, and future experiment to produce an Irish wolfdog type. Four MathML halves verified in P4 and P6; raw 12 is not twelve. Mastiff grandfather and superficial indistinguishability do not demonstrate that all established deerhounds share that ancestry or that offspring breed true. Newspaper Tegetmeier collaboration claim is second-hand and corrected in March 15 reply. Undated Darwin marks separate.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1843: March 15, supplied 1856; all seven blocks, eleven notes and bibliography read. P1 explicitly responds to Fox hound report, asks whether pure breed and reconstructed cross breed true and admits never seeing the breed. P2 thanks poultry efforts and reports recently examined Cochin, with separate translation work; Cochin came from Brent per apparatus, not necessarily Fox. P3 answers Tegetmeier report: he was not authorised to use Darwin name and their projects are not joint. P4 accepts specific Sebright offer. Preserved young specimens not yet examined. Later vertebral correction in Variation does not rewrite present claim. London visit completed, future work expansive and uncertain.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1887: June 4, supplied 1856; all three blocks and sole note read. Dorking arrived this morning, presumed from Fox; sender uncertain in body. Future skeleton preparation, not already performed. No incoming cover supplied, so specimen receipt does not establish March 8 as prompt. No bibliography section.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1895: Day 8 with June 1856 supplied; all seven blocks, twelve notes and bibliography read. Explicitly distinguishes earlier cock receipt acknowledgement from now-received missing Fox letter. Wife pregnancy tentative in current prose; later birth not imported. Brooke assistance heard this morning, Murray reports birds on road, East Africa shipment also prospective rather than received. Rabbit skeleton comparisons, duck queries and uncertain origin. Lyell earlier oral advice plus subsequent written pressure to publish preliminary essay now acted on; 1862 is surviving distinctive written witness, already known by May reply. Cat claim is uncertain and permission requested, not a settled biological finding. Later June 14 correction does not silently change blueish-grey wording. Future overseas letters not reconstructed.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1901: June 14, supplied 1856; all six blocks, five notes and bibliography read. Missing Fox reply corrects Darwin cats blunder, comments on proposed essay and supplies call-drake information. Original cat notes reportedly somewhere in large collection, not recovered here. Himalayan rabbit bespoken, not delivered. Asks half-bred duck fertility experiment, distinguishes pigeon crossing underway. Blackheath departure in ten minutes prospective. Neither earlier 1895 nor other Darwin outgoing can serve as incoming prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1967: October 3, supplied 1856; all nine blocks, seven notes and bibliography read. Missing Fox letter supplies illness and Anne grave news; showing Emma tonight is planned. Darwin chose not to revisit Malvern because grief might revive, while Moor Park only contemplated. Pregnancy, school and aunt injury contemporaneous; later chronology separate. Sketch abandoned for fuller book, still intends not to perfect every research line; reported Fox objections missing. Live Gambia birds received, call drake alive, habits and hawk-pellet delay newly requested. Land-mollusc eggs not obtained despite desire to test.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1978: October 20, supplied 1856; all nine blocks, seven notes and bibliography read. Missing Fox answers include family/school and health, not a surviving pea case. Eagle/owl seed pellets regurgitated after eighteen and sixteen hours with seeds apparently intact; germination still under test. Experimental-book quote in footnote has true sixteen and a quarter MathML hours and is a separate witness, not silent replacement of rounded body sixteen. Asks nephew to test lizard/snake eggs floating five or ten days; not experiment completed. December 19 pea material addresses public legume query, not this request.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-11799: December 19, supplied 1856, incomplete source; all four surviving blocks, six notes, annotations and bibliography read. Health update after Malvern is general continuity, not enough to identify a particular October question. P2 announces an enclosed answer but a section is excised, so author/topic/complete enclosure cannot be reconstructed. P3 quotes Gardeners Chronicle seed-growers claim; raw December 15/page 828 is corrected editorially to December 13/page 823 and both are preserved. P4 explicitly recalls Darwin legume enquiry the previous week and contrasts ten years of Queen Pea experience without deterioration. This answers public query 2012; no published newspaper response found does not exclude this private response. Later species-book insertion is not dated by the December 16 chapter completion, before this letter. Darwin annotations undated, quotation not Fox personal observation.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2049: February 8, supplied 1857; all thirteen blocks, nine notes and bibliography read. Current missing Fox note has no health news, so cannot be December 19 health letter. Sixth son birth nearly two months ago, Fox expected child jokingly three-quarters and total twenty and three-quarters: two actual three-quarter MathML nodes verified, not 34 or 2034 children. Future publication at least two years, not a fixed completed date. Helix pomatia survived fourteen days; orchid pollen and castrated deer are questions. West Indies thanks lacks recovered exact input, and enclosures not synthesized. Historical medical choices are author report.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2057: February 22, supplied 1857; all eight blocks, eight notes and bibliography read. Various enclosures and new baby news include missing contemporary inputs; December 19 source cannot explain February birth. P4 uniquely replies to Queen Pea grown beside other varieties in 11799 P4, asks simultaneous flowering and distinguishes observational bee inference from preponderating cultivation reports. P1 Gully benefit, P3 nephew eggs and P5 school query not uniquely assigned to December letter. Helix survival now twenty days, distinct from earlier fourteen-day stage. Wife preference and fame/anonymity reflection are Darwin prose, not evidence results or actual publication anonymity.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2085: Supplied April 30, 1857, Thursday; all four blocks, nine notes and bibliography read. Date relies on postmark plus stated exactly one week at Moor Park, while journal records April 22 arrival; preserve both and do not silently infer April 23. Improvement is personal report; comparisons with Gully and medical theory remain attributed historical beliefs. Enclosed establishment paper not recovered. Malvern family summer move is prospective and did not occur per later diary. P3 requests facts about crossed Chinese/Neapolitan pig breeds breeding true, not an observation supplied by Fox. Wednesday next routing instruction historical.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2161: October 30, supplied 1857; all eight blocks, twelve notes and bibliography read. Missing Fox note asks school/family. Darwin now attributes benefit primarily to stopping mental work, hydropathy only secondarily, unlike April emphasis; preserve changing views. Lane booklet read favourably, proposed move not completed until 1860. Henrietta return Saturday is future relative October 30, later diary confirms October 31. Two draft chapters in six months, not whole book complete. School preference Rugby lacks articulated reason and does not imply enrolment. House extension and fruit-tree results reported, future Catherine move uncertain.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1728: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Day 22 with July 1855 supplied. White Dorking seven-day specimen received, others promised; own two ten-day pigeons prepared. Historical specimen-preparation description remains source prose, not instructions to the research agent. Raw P2 MathML is one-half hour, not flattened twelve. Missing Fox mongrel letter includes scolding joke and lineage ideas; prior oral retriever facts separately noted. Asks precise evidence for eight-generation bulldog trace, setter origin and Lord Hill Dorking cross rather than asserting each proved. P9 Atriplex germinated this morning after 100 days. Later Variation citations are future apparatus.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1733: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. July 31 with supplied 1855 year. Cochin, call duck and Sebright Bantam physically received safely; subvariety identity remains a question. Apparatus calls fowls eight-day-old while earlier request/receipt refers to seven-day birds; body itself gives no age, so do not assign an exact uniform age to all received specimens from apparatus. Poultry show attendance planned. Wood extract received but whole book will be obtained; Bewick work newly mentioned and will be checked, not yet read. Fox monophyletic dog argument ascribed through editorial inference; Dixon aboriginal-creation view is reported objection, not Darwin adoption. Four named seed kinds now germinated after 100 days; no inferred universal success percentage.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1745: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. August 22 with supplied 1855 year. Splendaceous Dorking received this morning, differs in colour but further distinguishing traits asked. P1–7 list the specimens received; raw HTML contains diag and Bantamramme fragments with no image/table. Missing Fox letter seems to claim Spanish chick sent; Darwin expressly has not received it, distinct from old Spanish cock from uncertain Mr Wilmot. Other adult specimens still wanted; rumpless fowls and four pigeon races obtained. P8 neighbour inquiry pending, P13 postscript now can get Spanish chicken, not evidence chick physically delivered. Worker summary completing pigeon collection/obtaining Spanish overstates these stages.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1766: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. October 14 with supplied 1855 year dated by correspondence. Game chick received this morning, juvenile collection sufficient for intended comparison but results not yet produced. After missing last Fox note Darwin wrote Mrs Wilmot thanks; this later name resolution does not retroactively settle uncertain August Mr Wilmot. Old Dorking/Cochin/call duck still wanted, excellent game accessible. Glasgow BAAS meeting and Shrewsbury visit completed; Egerton exchange oral, Argyll speech heard but no inference of reading printed report. Hore letter received roughly two months ago states he quit natural history; source not located and no exact receipt day assigned. Both adult request list P2–4 and pigeon inventory P10–18 contain literal diag/ramme damage in raw HTML; retain order and punctuation pending authoritative rendering.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2012: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Pinned prior primary full-source and full-body reading reused. Before December6,1856 request for evidence on leguminous crossing, with conflicting contemporary views including Gärtner1849. No published response located per apparatus. Evidence preponderates against crossing is provisional1856 assessment, not reconciled backwards from2359 experiments.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1862: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. May 1–2, 1856, fifteen retained blocks, full annotations, all seventeen notes and bibliography read. May 1 text was expressly not posted that day; May 2 addition precedes sending. Earlier shell list is missing, and corrected nomenclature/Helix rufescens question mark do not reconstruct it. Woodward/Prentice beetle carrying Ancylus and Curtis spider eggs on Dytiscus are relayed reports, not Lyell or Darwin direct observations of those cases. Nanina name list has raw diag/ramme fragments and no restored table layout. J.E. Gray is the reported classifier, not Asa. Heer lending is future while Lyell still uses the paper; later August reading is not May access. P6 expressly urges a small species-theory publication; May 2 P14 retains Lyell specific-centre hypothesis. Undated Darwin annotations are separate from letter prose and do not fix receipt.

reading_method: Root independently read complete surviving new source bodies, metadata constraints, exclusions, footnotes, scholarly sections and bibliography. Actual special markup and figures inspected where present. Reused explicit accepted primary readings only after matching source and accepted evidence hashes. Historical decisions and notes are handwritten; validation packages evidence rather than adjudicating it.
